// diagnostic

E1008

Binary pattern read needs/misuses an endian suffix — multi-byte read without `be`/`le`, or `le`/`be` on a single-byte or non-byte-multiple read (D-BINPAT1)

What

Binary pattern read needs/misuses an endian suffix — multi-byte read without `be`/`le`, or `le`/`be` on a single-byte or non-byte-multiple read (D-BINPAT1)

Why

The registered parse rule applies here

Fix

Follow the guidance for E1008

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E1008: tests/ui/binpat_multibyte_needs_endian.stderr.

Error [E1008]: `{…:U16}` reads more than one byte, so it needs a byte order
  --> tests/ui/binpat_multibyte_needs_endian.jet:4:20
    |
  4 |         [U8]{"{len:U16}"} -> { print("len {len}") }
    |                    ^^^
 Why: a read wider than 8 bits spans multiple bytes; Jet won't guess big- vs little-endian
 Fix: write `U16be` (big-endian / network order) or `U16le` (little-endian)
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E1008
